title: Best Heavy Duty Dehumidifier (2026): High-Capacity Picks
dek: When a 50-pint box can't keep up, these are the biggest dehumidifiers you can order, and what their giant pint numbers really mean.
description: The best heavy duty dehumidifier picks: high-capacity 100- to 240-pint units with pumps, plus how to read pint ratings, size up and plan power and drainage.
intro: A **heavy duty dehumidifier** is what you reach for when a standard 50-pint unit runs nonstop and the space still feels damp: a big unfinished basement, a whole lower level, a shop, a barn or a room drying out after a leak. Our top pick is the **AlorAir 170 PPD LGR**, a low-grain refrigerant machine with a built-in pump and a six-year limited warranty that gives homeowners and small contractors real headroom without stepping up to a restoration-company budget.

This guide ranks the biggest **high-capacity dehumidifiers** sold on Amazon by what you actually get for the money. Three things matter most: **how the capacity is rated** (a 240-pint headline and a 50-pint DOE rating are measured at very different conditions), **drainage** (a big unit can fill a bucket in an hour or two, so you need a pump or hose), and **power** (all of these run on a standard 115-volt outlet, but not every circuit can carry one alongside other loads).
topPicksLead: The **AlorAir 170 PPD LGR** is the best heavy-duty dehumidifier for most buyers, combining LGR drying, a built-in pump and a long warranty.

We don't run a test lab. We compare published capacity ratings and the conditions behind them (DOE 2019, AHAM or saturation), ENERGY STAR listings, coverage claims, drainage, warranty terms and CPSC recall records, then read owner reviews for durability and pump reliability.

blocks.caption: Headline capacities are manufacturer figures measured at warm, humid conditions; real output in a 65–70°F basement is lower.

sections.heading: How to choose a heavy-duty dehumidifier

items.label: Read the rating conditions
items.text: Three different tests produce three very different numbers.
sub: DOE 2019 (65°F, 60% RH): the residential standard, and the most conservative
AHAM (80°F, 60% RH): common for LGR and commercial units
Saturation (roughly 90–95°F, 90%+ RH): the biggest number, rarely seen in a home

items.label: Size for your space, not the box
items.text: Most homes need far less than 150 pints. Run the numbers in our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/), and consider a [100-pint class unit](/best/best-100-pint-dehumidifier/) before jumping to commercial gear.

items.label: Plan drainage first
items.text: A heavy-duty unit can fill a tank quickly. Choose a built-in pump if the drain is higher than the unit or far away, or a gravity hose if there's a floor drain below it.

items.label: LGR for dry-outs
items.text: Low-grain refrigerant units keep removing water as the air gets drier, which is what you want after a leak or flood. Our [LGR dehumidifier](/best/best-lgr-dehumidifier/) guide explains the difference.

items.label: Check the plug and circuit
items.text: All of these run on 115 volts, but read the nameplate amps and make sure the circuit isn't already carrying a freezer, sump pump or space heater.

items.label: Running cost
items.text: Bigger machines draw more power per hour, though a properly sized one runs fewer hours. Our [electricity guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) shows how to estimate the bill.

sections.heading: Why a "150-pint" dehumidifier might only be a 50-pint

blocks.text: Since 2019, residential portables have been rated by the DOE at 65°F and 60% humidity, cooler and drier than the old test. That's why the old "70-pint" class became today's 50-pint class. Many big-box listings, though, still lead with numbers measured in hot, saturated air.

The difference can be dramatic. Waykar's CTH150PD, sold as a 150-pint unit, carries a DOE rating of about 49 pints on its ENERGY STAR listing, and the CHWA80A, sold as an 80-pint, is rated at about 25 DOE pints. The numbers simply describe different weather. When a unit is ENERGY STAR certified, look up its DOE figure and size on that.

blocks.title: A quick rule of thumb
blocks.text: Halve a saturation rating to estimate AHAM output, and expect less again in a cool basement. If you need true 100+ pint AHAM performance, look for a unit that publishes an AHAM number.

A standard 15-amp household circuit can carry about 12 amps of continuous load, and a 20-amp circuit about 16. A large dehumidifier running for days counts as continuous, so plug it into a circuit with little else on it, ideally a dedicated one.

items: **Avoid extension cords when you can.** Most manuals advise plugging straight into a grounded wall outlet.
**If you must use one,** keep it short, grounded, outdoor-rated in damp spaces and heavy gauge (12 AWG for most heavy-duty units), rated above the unit's amps.
**Use GFCI protection** in basements, garages and anywhere near water.
**Never daisy-chain** power strips or cords to reach a big unit.
**A large, wet basement or occasional water-damage dry-outs:** the AlorAir 170 PPD LGR.
**The biggest open space you can imagine, or you want a 30-gallon unit:** the Moiswell 240-Pint.
**A cool basement or crawl space with no low drain:** the Airzentti 155-Pint.
**A shop or basement with a floor drain right there:** the Waykar 155-Pint on a gravity hose.
**A finished lower level where you want app control and a home-appliance look:** the Costway 100-Pint.
**A one-time flood:** consider [renting](/guides/dehumidifier-rental/) a pro LGR for a few days instead of buying.

blocks.text: The best high-capacity dehumidifier is the one whose real rating, drainage and power needs fit your space. The AlorAir 170 PPD LGR is our pick for most heavy-duty jobs, the Moiswell 240 is the biggest you can order, the Airzentti and Waykar 155-pint units cover pump and gravity setups, and the Costway 100-Pint suits a lived-in lower level. Read the rating conditions, plan the drain, check the circuit, and you'll get the drying power you're paying for.

faqs.q: What is the largest dehumidifier you can buy?
faqs.a: For plug-in units sold online, the Moiswell 240-Pint is among the largest, rated at 240 pints (30 gallons) a day under maximum conditions. Truly larger systems are ducted or industrial units installed by contractors.
Yes, in the sense that 30 gallons equals 240 pints, which is the Moiswell 240-Pint's headline rating. That figure is measured in hot, saturated air, so expect considerably less in a typical basement.

faqs.q: Do I need a heavy-duty dehumidifier for my basement?
faqs.a: Usually not. A 50-pint unit with a pump or hose handles most basements up to about 2,500 square feet. Step up to a heavy-duty unit if a 50-pint runs nonstop and can't reach 50%, the space is very large, or you're drying out after water damage.

faqs.q: How big a dehumidifier do I need?
faqs.a: It depends on square footage and how damp the space is. A moderately damp 1,500 sq ft basement needs about 35–50 DOE pints; a wet 2,500 sq ft space or a dry-out calls for more. Our size guide walks through the math.

faqs.q: Can I use an extension cord with a heavy-duty dehumidifier?
faqs.a: It's best to plug straight into a grounded outlet. If you can't, use a short, grounded, heavy-gauge cord (12 AWG for most large units) rated above the dehumidifier's amps, with GFCI protection in damp areas.

faqs.q: Is the Eva-Dry E-500 a high-capacity dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Only by mini-dehumidifier standards. The E-500 is a renewable silica-gel unit for closets, boats and cabinets that holds 6–8 ounces per charge. For a room or basement you need a compressor unit; see our [Eva-Dry guide](/best/best-eva-dry-dehumidifier/) for where it fits.

faqs.q: Should I rent or buy a heavy-duty dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Rent for a one-time flood or leak that needs a few days of drying. Buy if you'll use it every season, own rental property or do regular renovation work, since the rental cost adds up quickly.
